Trace one transition across lags

Source: R/lsa-lags.R
lag_profile.Rd

lag_profile() traces one from -> to transition across lags, one row per lag with the count, the transition probability, the adjusted residual and its p-value. This lag profile shows how the association between two states changes with the distance between them: whether a transition that is over-represented at lag 1 persists, decays or reverses at lags 2, 3 and beyond (Sackett, 1979). For example, it shows whether disengagement is still unlikely several time points after an active one, or only at the next.

lag_profile() fits the lags itself from raw data, or reads an existing lsa_lags() result.

Usage

lag_profile(x, from, to, lags = 1:3, ...)

Arguments

x

Sequences in any form accepted by lsa(), or an lsa_lags() result.

from, to

State names of the transition.

lags

Integer vector of lags (default 1:3); ignored when x is an lsa_lags result.

...

Passed to lsa_lags() when x is raw data.

Value

A data.frame with one row per lag and the columns lag, from, to, count, prob, adj_res, p and significant.

Conditions

Errors carry the class lagdynamics_error and lagdynamics_bad_input when from or to is not a state of the data.

References

Sackett, G. P. (1979). The lag sequential analysis of contingency and cyclicity in behavioral interaction research. In J. D. Osofsky (Ed.), Handbook of infant development (pp. 623-649). Wiley.

See also

lsa_lags(), transitions()

Examples

lag_profile(engagement, from = "Active", to = "Disengaged", lags = 1:4)
#>   lag   from         to count       prob    adj_res            p significant
#> 1   1 Active Disengaged    23 0.03495441 -12.556925 3.642124e-36        TRUE
#> 2   2 Active Disengaged    33 0.05357143 -10.648529 1.771422e-26        TRUE
#> 3   3 Active Disengaged    35 0.06151142  -9.416031 4.684613e-21        TRUE
#> 4   4 Active Disengaged    39 0.07617188  -7.937923 2.055951e-15        TRUE
